html:
In a referendum on 14 June 1993, Malawians voted by about two to one to end one-party rule under Hastings Banda and allow rival parties.

A pastoral letter read in Catholic churches in 1992, criticising the regime, set off protests and strikes. Foreign donors froze aid, and Banda, in his nineties, agreed to the vote.

In the election of May 1994, Bakili Muluzi of the United Democratic Front won the presidency, and Banda conceded. A new constitution followed. Malawi has since had several changes of government by election, and in 2020 its courts annulled a flawed presidential vote, a rare event in Africa, completing the work begun in Lilongwe in 1993.
sum: In a referendum on 14 June 1993, Malawians voted by about two to one to end one-party rule under Hastings Banda and allow rival parties.
